entry.title: KTM24 v Rio Tinto Limited (Strike Out) [2026] FCA 1579
entry.content:
Rio Tinto applied to strike out parts of representative proceedings brought by the applicants alleging sexual harassment and sex discrimination in employment. The Federal Court struck out certain paragraphs of the pleadings for lack of material facts but granted leave to amend the group member definition and other pleadings, finding the applicants largely successful. Costs were awarded to the applicants as the overall successful party on the interlocutory applications.

Federal Court of Australia, 23 Oct 2026, [2026] FCA 1579

entry.title: XSLP and Telstra Corporation Limited (Practice and procedure) [2026] ARTA 2415
entry.content:
In XSLP and Telstra Corporation Limited (Practice and procedure) [2026] ARTA 2415, the Tribunal dealt with suppression orders made in XSLP’s compensation review and later discrimination/Federal Court proceedings. It varied a commercial-in-confidence order over Telstra documents by consent, continued an order protecting XSLP’s identity, and clarified that the parties could use evidence and reasons in Federal Court subject to those orders.

Key holding: Under the ART Act, the s 70 power to restrict publication or disclosure requires a mandatory s 71(2) weighing exercise, including all statutory considerations, before it can be exercised.

When considering whether to make an order under s 70, the weighing exercise required under s 71(2) is an essential prerequisite of the power to do so. In that exercise, the Tribunal must have regard to all the mandatory considerations in paragraphs 71(2)(a) to (e).

Administrative Review Tribunal, 6 Oct 2026, [2026] ARTA 2415
